group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-03 (tool=LEGEND-research): 'Chang NS[au]' 138, 'Chang NS[au] AND WWOX' 66, 'Hsu LJ[au]' 103, 'Hsu LJ[au] AND WWOX' 30.
group_assessment.weighting: Five of the six papers in this group come from one laboratory lineage (Chang N-S / Hsu L-J, National Cheng Kung University). That laboratory originated WWOX and carries the gene's largest single output, so its measurements carry full weight; what it does NOT carry is independence. Two of its subjects are exclusive to it: 'Zfra NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 1 record and that record is an unrelated zebrafish androgen-receptor paper matching the string by accident; 'TIAF1 NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 5 of 20. The autophagy axis is the opposite case and is the reason this group is readable as a contradiction at all: 'WWOX AND autophagy' returns 10 records and 8 of them are from neither Chang NS nor Hsu LJ.
group_assessment.note: Research-group knowledge base is excluded from the public edition; this rests on measured PubMed counts and on the papers' own author lists.

multihop.enumeration_method: 38 <ref> elements, 39 PMIDs present in the deposit (the deposit also carries the PMID of one related-article notice). Gene-directedness was not classified; that is triage work and is deferred.
multihop.dedup_performed: Not performed as a list; the one integrity-relevant reference was checked by hand (see corpus_crossquery).

corpus_crossquery.query: Does the deposit carry an integrity notice on anything this paper depends on, and is the paper's own supplement retrievable?
corpus_crossquery.finding: Two findings. (1) The deposited reference list carries a related-article notice of type expression-of-concern on reference 15 (Fabbri et al. 2005, PNAS, WWOX gene restoration; the notice is deposited as PMC5402418). The expression of concern is on a work this paper cites in its introduction, not on this paper. (2) The supplementary PDF deposited for this article is NOT this article's supplement: the same bytes (sha256 dc13d0427a4777bf4e09661df3e6cab669f005edb232adbc5d2cb4bda957004f) are served by two independent routes - the PMC OA S3 open-data bucket and the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint - and both carry five figures of an unrelated haematology study. Supplementary Figures 1-7 of this paper, including Supplementary Figure 7 (the Wwox+/- and Wwox-/- MEF LC3-II arm), are therefore not retrievable from the deposit.

retraction_check.route: PubMed efetch CommentsCorrections, plus a scan of the JATS deposit for related-article elements
retraction_check.result: No retraction, no expression of concern and no erratum on PMID 24008736 itself. The deposit does carry an expression-of-concern notice attached to its reference 15 (a cited work).

entries.proposition: THE FLUX CLAMP EXISTS AND IT IS ON THE DRUG, NOT ON WWOX. E64d plus pepstatin A were used to exclude accelerated lysosomal turnover as the explanation of the LC3-II loss - but the clamped comparison is MTX versus no MTX, with no WWOX manipulation in the clamped arm. The sign of the WWOX-to-autophagy step is therefore never measured under a flux clamp anywhere in this paper.
entries.snippet: the presence of E64d and pepstatin A did not prevent MTX-induced downregulation of LC3 protein expression
entries.anchor: Results, 'MTX modulates autophagy in SCC cells', LC3 paragraph

experimental_context.treatment: MTX 10 ug/ml with or without E64d 30 uM + pepstatin A 15 uM

entries.proposition: THE mTOR ARM IS A PHYSICAL INTERACTION PLUS A PHOSPHORYLATION CORRELATION, AND THE AUTHORS STATE THE CAUSAL ORDER AS A POSSIBILITY. No rapamycin or raptor arm separates mTOR from the autophagy readout.
entries.snippet: raising the possibility that WWOX may regulate autophagy through mTOR activation in MTX-treated SCC-15 cells
entries.anchor: Results, 'MTX treatment modulates mTOR signaling in SCC cells via WWOX', final sentence

entries.proposition: THE ONE LOSS-OF-FUNCTION ARM THAT REACHES OUTSIDE THE ONCOLOGY STRESS CONTEXT IS A SINGLE SENTENCE POINTING AT A SUPPLEMENTARY FIGURE THAT THE DEPOSIT DOES NOT CARRY. It is also the only arm of this paper in which a germline Wwox genotype, rather than a drug, is the variable - which is exactly the arm a WWOX-DEE genotype class could inherit.
entries.snippet: In our recently developed Wwox gene knockout mouse embryonic fibroblasts, increased expression of LC3-II protein was detected in the cytosolic protein extracts from the Wwox+/− and Wwox−/− cells using western blotting, as compared with the Wwox+/+ control cells
entries.anchor: Results, 'WWOX suppresses autophagy in SCC cells', third sentence

entries.proposition: THE LC3 LOSS IS ROUTED TO THE PROTEASOME, NOT TO THE LYSOSOME, IN THIS SAME CELL LINE. That matters for the group's own later paper, which routes Bcl-XL and Mcl-1 degradation to the lysosome in the same SCC-15 background: the two routes are different cargo in one cell type, not one mechanism stated twice.
entries.snippet: Treatment of SCC-15 cells with a proteasome inhibitor MG132 blocked MTX-induced LC3 protein downregulation, indicating that LC3 protein is degraded via the ubiquitin/proteasomal pathway post MTX treatment
entries.anchor: Results, 'MTX modulates autophagy in SCC cells', LC3 paragraph, final sentence

entries.proposition: THE PAPER'S OWN SCOPE SENTENCE BINDS THE DIRECTION TO A DRUG, A TUMOUR AND AN APOPTOTIC ENDPOINT. A registry gloss that carries 'WWOX suppresses autophagy' without this clause has promoted a scoped result to an unscoped one.
entries.snippet: Thus, WWOX suppresses autophagy for inducing apoptosis in MTX-treated human SCC.
